statement:
In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, a morphism of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** when every Yoneda test $h_U\to G$ has scheme-representable fibre product $h_U\times_GF$. For a property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms preserved under arbitrary base change and fppf-local on the base, $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ precisely if all resulting scheme maps $V_\xi\to U$ have $\mathcal P$. A surjective representable morphism means surjective on such scheme tests; this is distinguished from surjectivity as a presheaf map.

Let $S$, $X$, $Y$ be objects of $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of schemes.
Let $\mathcal{P}$ be as in
Definition \ref{definition-relative-representable-property}.
Then $h_X \longrightarrow h_Y$ has property $\mathcal{P}$ if
and only if $f$ has property $\mathcal{P}$.

statement:
In the chosen big fppf site over a base scheme $S$, a morphism of presheaves $a:F\to G$ is **representable** when every Yoneda test $h_U\to G$ has scheme-representable fibre product $h_U\times_GF$. For a property $\mathcal P$ of scheme morphisms preserved under arbitrary base change and fppf-local on the base, $a$ has property $\mathcal P$ precisely if all resulting scheme maps $V_\xi\to U$ have $\mathcal P$. A surjective representable morphism means surjective on such scheme tests; this is distinguished from surjectivity as a presheaf map.

Let $S$ be a scheme contained in $\Sch_{fppf}$.
Let $F$ be a presheaf of sets on $(\Sch/S)_{fppf}$.
The following are equivalent:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the diagonal $F \to F \times F$ is representable,
\item for $U \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$ and any $a \in F(U)$
the map $a : h_U \to F$ is representable,
\item for every pair $U, V \in \Ob((\Sch/S)_{fppf})$
and any $a \in F(U)$, $b \in F(V)$ the fibre product
$h_U \times_{a, F, b} h_V$ is representable.
\end{enumerate}
